title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, numbered 154 of Exposé IX, from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §12.3. It sits between handwritten pages on semi-simplicial sets and topos cohomology, which suggests it was reused or misfiled.

Setting: C is a proper curve over an algebraically closed field (in SGA 7 IX, the special fibre of a semistable or regular model). π: C̃ → C is its normalization. The connected component Pic^0_C is an extension of an abelian variety by a linear group whose toric part is T. M = D(T) is the character group of T, and R = M^∨ is its dual.

The page states the combinatorial description of M through the dual graph Γ(C) (Bourbaki, Lie, Ch. IV, Annexe):
- Vertices are the irreducible components C̃_i of C̃.
- Edges between C̃_i and C̃_j correspond to unordered pairs of distinct branches through a common point. For i≠j this set is C̃_i ×_C C̃_j. For i=j it is (C̃_i ×_C C̃_i − Δ) modulo the symmetry, which is empty when C_i is unibranch.

Claim (12.3.7): M = D(T) ≅ H_1(Γ(C), ℤ), hence R ≅ H^1(Γ(C), ℤ). Only the map H_1 → M is to be defined; that it is an isomorphism is left to the reader.

To set this up, let I be the set of points of C lying on at least two branches, J the set of irreducible components, and K = π^{-1}(I) the set of branches at points of I. Let h = (f, g): K → I × J send a branch to its point and its component. Then (12.3.10) recasts the earlier description (12.3.4) as M ≅ Ker(ℤ^{(K)} → ...).

This comes from the units sequence 1 → O_C^* → π_*O_{C̃}^* → ⊕_{x∈I} (∏_{branches} G_m)/G_m → .... It gives T = coker(G_m^J → ∏_x G_m^{K_x}/G_m). Its characters are the integer vectors on K whose sum over the branches at each x vanishes and whose sum over the branches on each component j vanishes. That is the kernel of the boundary map ℤ^K → ℤ^I ⊕ ℤ^J of the bipartite graph with vertex set I ⊔ J and edge set K. This bipartite graph is homotopy-equivalent (after subdividing) to Γ(C), so its H_1 equals H_1(Γ(C)).
errors: The target of (12.3.10) is written ℤ^{(I×J)}. Read literally, as the free group on the product set pushed forward along h, the kernel is wrong. Counterexample: two smooth components meeting transversally at two points. Then ℤ^K → ℤ^{I×J} is bijective, so the kernel is 0, but H_1(Γ) has rank 1. The correct target is ℤ^{(I)} ⊕ ℤ^{(J)}, with the map (ℤ^{(f)}, ℤ^{(g)}). The notation 'I×J' should be read as this product of free modules, not the free module on I×J.
The direction of the isomorphism arrows is a bit inconsistent between M and R. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Character group of the toric part of Pic^0 of a degenerate curve is H_1 of its dual graph; dually R ≅ H^1(Γ, ℤ).
ideas.modern_name: Dual graph of a nodal/semistable curve; toric rank = first Betti number of the dual graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX §12.3); also Raynaud; folklore in degeneration theory

ideas.what: Presentation of M as the kernel of the boundary map of the bipartite incidence graph (points ⊔ components, edges = branches) via h = (f, g): K → I × J.
ideas.modern_name: Cycle space of the incidence (bipartite) graph

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, apparently misplaced among the 1975–76 notes. Its content is published and well known. The only point of interest is the misleading notation ℤ^{(I×J)} in (12.3.10).
transcription_corrections: Page header '- 154 - IX' and the archive number 472 indicate SGA 7 Exposé IX, page 154. This is a typescript, not part of the handwritten de Rham notes.
The machine transcription of the arrows in (12.3.7) and (12.3.10) is approximate. The image shows '≃' with arrows: M = D(T) ←≃ H_1(Γ(C),ℤ) and M^∨ = R ≃→ H^1(Γ(C),ℤ).
'appartenant a au moins' should read 'appartenant à au moins'. The original typescript has the accent missing.
